SLIDE — Movement Technique (Common)

While sprinting, dropping low converts speed into a controlled slide along the ground, fueled by a burst of energy rather than stamina.

A Slide lets a runner pass beneath an obstacle too low to duck under while standing, or beneath a swing aimed where your head used to be.

It only works at speed — sliding from a standstill accomplishes nothing but looking foolish.

Energy spent here is energy not available for anything else. Use it when the gap is real, not out of habit.
